lines.raw: Two big families: people and organizations.

scenes.section: Two big families: people and organizations

lines.raw: The first split is simple: a provider is either a **person** or an **organization**.
lines.say: The first split is simple: a provider is either a person or an organization.

lines.raw: In US data this split is so important that the NPI itself records it as **Type 1** or **Type 2**.
lines.say: In U S data this split is so important that the N P I itself records it as Type 1 or Type 2.

scenes.section: Two big families: people and organizations

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: Who gets it. Type 1 NPI: individual: A person who gives care: doctor, nurse practitioner, dentist, therapist, pharmacist. Type 2 NPI: organization: A business that gives care: hospital, clinic, doctors' group, lab, pharmacy, nursing home.
lines.say: Who gets it. Type 1 N P I: individual: A person who gives care: doctor, nurse practitioner, dentist, therapist, pharmacist. Type 2 N P I: organization: A business that gives care: hospital, clinic, doctors' group, lab, pharmacy, nursing home.

lines.raw: How many. Type 1 NPI: individual: **One per person, for life.** It stays the same if she moves state or changes job. Type 2 NPI: organization: One or more. A big hospital may have separate NPIs for different parts (subparts).
lines.say: How many. Type 1 N P I: individual: One per person, for life. It stays the same if she moves state or changes job. Type 2 N P I: organization: One or more. A big hospital may have separate N P I's for different parts (subparts).

lines.raw: Emily examples. Type 1 NPI: individual: Dr. Patel, Dr. Lee, Dr. Gomez. Type 2 NPI: organization: Sunrise Family Clinic, Lakeside General Hospital, Lakeside Surgical Group, Main Street Pharmacy.
lines.say: Emily examples. Type 1 N P I: individual: Doctor Patel, Doctor Lee, Doctor Gomez. Type 2 N P I: organization: Sunrise Family Clinic, Lakeside General Hospital, Lakeside Surgical Group, Main Street Pharmacy.

lines.raw: Usual claim role. Type 1 NPI: individual: **Rendering** (did the work). Type 2 NPI: organization: **Billing** (gets paid).
lines.say: Usual claim role. Type 1 N P I: individual: Rendering (did the work). Type 2 N P I: organization: Billing (gets paid).

lines.raw: Nepal comparison. Type 1 NPI: individual: A doctor's **NMC number**. Type 2 NPI: organization: A hospital's **registration** and **PAN**.
lines.say: Nepal comparison. Type 1 N P I: individual: A doctor's N M C number. Type 2 N P I: organization: A hospital's registration and P A N.

lines.raw: A doctor working alone.
lines.say: A doctor working alone.

lines.raw: A doctor who runs a one-person practice, not set up as a company, can bill with her own **Type 1** NPI.
lines.say: A doctor who runs a one-person practice, not set up as a company, can bill with her own Type 1 N P I.

lines.raw: If she sets up a company for her practice, the company gets its own **Type 2** NPI.
lines.say: If she sets up a company for her practice, the company gets its own Type 2 N P I.

lines.raw: So in data, a Type 1 NPI can sometimes appear as the **billing** provider too.
lines.say: So in data, a Type 1 N P I can sometimes appear as the billing provider too.

lines.raw: Kinds of individual providers.
lines.say: Kinds of individual providers.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Physician (MD or DO)**. What they do: Fully trained doctor. MD and DO doctors have the same rights to treat and prescribe. Nepal comparison: MBBS doctor, registered with NMC.
lines.say: Physician (M D or D O). What they do: Fully trained doctor. M D and D O doctors have the same rights to treat and prescribe. Nepal comparison: M B B S doctor, registered with N M C.

lines.raw: **Nurse practitioner (NP)**. What they do: Advanced nurse who can examine, diagnose and prescribe (rules differ by state). Nepal comparison: No exact match; closest is a senior staff nurse with extra training.
lines.say: Nurse practitioner (N P). What they do: Advanced nurse who can examine, diagnose and prescribe (rules differ by state). Nepal comparison: No exact match; closest is a senior staff nurse with extra training.

lines.raw: **Physician assistant (PA)**. What they do: Works with doctors, examines and treats patients. Nepal comparison: Somewhat like a health assistant (HA) in a health post.
lines.say: Physician assistant (P A). What they do: Works with doctors, examines and treats patients. Nepal comparison: Somewhat like a health assistant (H A) in a health post.

lines.raw: **Dentist, optometrist, therapist**. What they do: Teeth, eyes, physiotherapy, mental health and more. Nepal comparison: Dental surgeon, eye clinic staff, physiotherapist.
lines.say: Dentist, optometrist, therapist. What they do: Teeth, eyes, physiotherapy, mental health and more. Nepal comparison: Dental surgeon, eye clinic staff, physiotherapist.

lines.raw: **Pharmacist**. What they do: Dispenses medicines. Nepal comparison: Pharmacist registered with the Nepal Pharmacy Council.
lines.say: Pharmacist. What they do: Dispenses medicines. Nepal comparison: Pharmacist registered with the Nepal Pharmacy Council.

lines.raw: Kinds of organizations (facilities).
lines.say: Kinds of organizations (facilities).

lines.raw: A **facility** is a place where care happens.
lines.say: A facility is a place where care happens.

lines.raw: Facilities usually send **institutional** claims (UB-04), while doctors' groups send **professional** claims (CMS-1500).
lines.say: Facilities usually send institutional claims (U B 04), while doctors' groups send professional claims (C M S 1500).

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Acute care hospital**. What happens there: Emergency care, surgery, overnight stays. Nepal comparison: A big private hospital or a government hospital in Kathmandu.
lines.say: Acute care hospital. What happens there: Emergency care, surgery, overnight stays. Nepal comparison: A big private hospital or a government hospital in Kathmandu.

lines.raw: **Critical access hospital**. What happens there: A small rural hospital with a few beds, given special Medicare rules. Nepal comparison: A district hospital far from the city.
lines.say: Critical access hospital. What happens there: A small rural hospital with a few beds, given special Medicare rules. Nepal comparison: A district hospital far from the city.

lines.raw: **Ambulatory surgery center (ASC)**. What happens there: Same-day surgery, patient goes home the same day. Nepal comparison: A day-care surgery unit.
lines.say: Ambulatory surgery center (A S C). What happens there: Same-day surgery, patient goes home the same day. Nepal comparison: A day-care surgery unit.

lines.raw: **Clinic / physician office**. What happens there: Check-ups, small illnesses, follow-ups. Nepal comparison: A polyclinic or a doctor's private chamber.
lines.say: Clinic or physician office. What happens there: Check-ups, small illnesses, follow-ups. Nepal comparison: A polyclinic or a doctor's private chamber.

lines.raw: **Urgent care center**. What happens there: Walk-in care for problems that cannot wait but are not emergencies. Nepal comparison: An evening OPD that takes walk-ins.
lines.say: Urgent care center. What happens there: Walk-in care for problems that cannot wait but are not emergencies. Nepal comparison: An evening O P D that takes walk-ins.

lines.raw: **Skilled nursing facility (SNF)**. What happens there: Nursing and rehab after a hospital stay. Nepal comparison: Rare in Nepal; family usually cares at home.
lines.say: Skilled nursing facility (S N F). What happens there: Nursing and rehab after a hospital stay. Nepal comparison: Rare in Nepal; family usually cares at home.

lines.raw: **Home health agency, hospice**. What happens there: Care at home; comfort care at the end of life. Nepal comparison: Home-care nursing services in cities.
lines.say: Home health agency, hospice. What happens there: Care at home; comfort care at the end of life. Nepal comparison: Home-care nursing services in cities.

lines.raw: **Laboratory, imaging center**. What happens there: Blood tests, X-rays, MRI scans. Nepal comparison: A pathology lab or diagnostic centre.
lines.say: Laboratory, imaging center. What happens there: Blood tests, X-rays, M R I scans. Nepal comparison: A pathology lab or diagnostic centre.

lines.raw: **Pharmacy**. What happens there: Dispenses medicines (see the Pharmacy course). Nepal comparison: A pharmacy registered with the Department of Drug Administration.
lines.say: Pharmacy. What happens there: Dispenses medicines (see the Pharmacy course). Nepal comparison: A pharmacy registered with the Department of Drug Administration.

lines.say: Both appear on his receipt.

lines.say: If Ram needs a blood test, he may go to a separate pathology lab: a third provider, with its own bill.

lines.raw: His private insurer cares about both: is the doctor registered with NMC, and is the hospital a genuine, licensed hospital?
lines.say: His private insurer cares about both: is the doctor registered with N M C, and is the hospital a genuine, licensed hospital?

lines.raw: With the Social Security Fund:
lines.say: With the Social Security Fund:

lines.raw: SSF lists **hospitals** (organizations), not individual doctors.
lines.say: S S F lists hospitals (organizations), not individual doctors.

lines.raw: The hospital is responsible for its doctors.
lines.say: The hospital is responsible for its doctors.

lines.raw: Sita can choose among SSF-listed hospitals; the treating doctor is recorded on her visit.
lines.say: Sita can choose among S S F listed hospitals; the treating doctor is recorded on her visit.

lines.raw: This is similar to a US network contract signed with a **group** or **hospital**, which then covers all its doctors.
lines.say: This is similar to a U S network contract signed with a group or hospital, which then covers all its doctors.

lines.raw: Specialties.
lines.say: Specialties.

lines.raw: Individual providers also have a **specialty**: the area of medicine they trained in.
lines.say: Individual providers also have a specialty: the area of medicine they trained in.

lines.raw: US doctors usually train for 3 to 7 years after medical school in their specialty, and many pass an exam to become **board certified**.
lines.say: U S doctors usually train for 3 to 7 years after medical school in their specialty, and many pass an exam to become board certified.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Primary care**. Specialty examples: Family medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics (children), sometimes OB/GYN. Emily's providers: Dr. Patel, family medicine.
lines.say: Primary care. Specialty examples: Family medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics (children), sometimes OB/GYN. Emily's providers: Doctor Patel, family medicine.

lines.raw: **Surgical**. Specialty examples: General surgery, orthopedics (bones), cardiothoracic surgery. Emily's providers: Dr. Lee, general surgeon.
lines.say: Surgical. Specialty examples: General surgery, orthopedics (bones), cardiothoracic surgery. Emily's providers: Doctor Lee, general surgeon.

lines.raw: **Medical specialists**. Specialty examples: Cardiology (heart), endocrinology (diabetes, hormones), oncology (cancer). Emily's providers: None yet.
lines.say: Medical specialists. Specialty examples: Cardiology (heart), endocrinology (diabetes, hormones), oncology (cancer). Emily's providers: None yet.

lines.raw: **Hospital-based**. Specialty examples: Anesthesiology, emergency medicine, radiology, pathology. Emily's providers: Dr. Gomez, anaesthesiologist.
lines.say: Hospital-based. Specialty examples: Anesthesiology, emergency medicine, radiology, pathology. Emily's providers: Doctor Gomez, anaesthesiologist.

lines.raw: In the US: Why specialty matters in US data.
lines.say: In the U S: Why specialty matters in U S data.

lines.raw: **Benefits**: many plans charge a lower copay for a **primary care** visit than for a **specialist** visit.
lines.say: Benefits: many plans charge a lower copay for a primary care visit than for a specialist visit.

lines.raw: **Payment**: insurers often pay different rates for the same service by specialty.
lines.say: Payment: insurers often pay different rates for the same service by specialty.

lines.raw: **Analysis**: "How much do we spend on cardiology?" needs a correct specialty on every provider.
lines.say: Analysis: "How much do we spend on cardiology?" needs a correct specialty on every provider.

lines.raw: **Attribution**: only primary care providers are usually counted when deciding who is a member's main doctor (lesson 6).
lines.say: Attribution: only primary care providers are usually counted when deciding who is a member's main doctor (lesson 6).

lines.raw: Specialty is like a shop's category.
lines.say: Specialty is like a shop's category.

lines.raw: On New Road, a shop might be a jeweller, a shoe shop or a mobile shop.
lines.say: On New Road, a shop might be a jeweller, a shoe shop or a mobile shop.

lines.raw: The **shop** is the provider; the **category** is its specialty.
lines.say: The shop is the provider; the category is its specialty.

lines.raw: Knowing the category lets you compare like with like: you would not compare a jeweller's prices with a shoe shop's.
lines.say: Knowing the category lets you compare like with like: you would not compare a jeweller's prices with a shoe shop's.
